To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we demonstrated 40-Gb and 80-Gbps all-optical demux using MZ switches with bi-directional pump, and we showed that the bi-directional configuration can increase a nonlinear phase shift and reduce a power penalty in comparison with the single pump case.
we demonstrated all-optical 160-to-40/80-Gb/s demultiplixing using a MZI all-optical switch based on intersubband transition in InGaAs coupled double quantum wells.

we demonstrated all-optical switching at 40/80 GHz with a Mach-Zehender interferometer, where the picoseconds cross-phase modulation ( XPM ) induced by intersub-band excitation of InGaAs /AlAsSb double quantum wells (DQW) is utilized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of all-optical demultiplixing devices based on intersubband transition of InGaAs quantum wells.
a development of all-optical signal processing devices based on intersubband XPM in quantum wells.
all-optical signal processing for high-speed optical communication networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bi-directional configuration is the effective method for the all-optical demultplexing with the current low XMP efficiency.
the bi-directional pumping is a very effective way to increase the nonlinear phase shift and to reduce power penalty in demultiplexing applications.
the bi-directional pumping is the effective and promising way to improve all-optical demux performance, especially at high repetition rate of 80GHz.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the bi-directional pumping scheme is effective to increase XPM efficiency, but it does not improve the power penalty in the case where a nonlinear phase shift is not enough to be obtained by a pump power.
the XPM efficiency and the damage threshold are two key factors to be improved to realize the all-optical demultplexing with low power penalty.

the all-optical demulti-plexing of 160 to 80-Gb/ s and 160 to 160-Gb/ s are demonstrated for the first time, which are based on XPM in InGaAs/AISASb coupled double quantum well and a bi-directional pump scheme, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the all-optical switching based on intersubband transitions in coupled double quantum wells has the potential for high-speed demultiplexing in the future.
the bi-directional pumping scheme is effective to increase the XPM efficiency by a factor of two, and it is a promising technique to realize a high-speed optical switch with high damage threshold.
the bi-directional control pulse injection is a promising technique to reduce a power penalty for the all-optical signal processing.
